text.p: Australian retailer Woolworths Ltd should announce another increase in net earnings for the half year ended December 31 when it reports on Monday, despite intense competition in the retail sector, analysts said.
Analysts expect the group to report a net profit of about A$145 million for the half year, up from A$135.8 million in 1995. This would represent a profit gain of 6.8 percent.
Profit forecasts among analysts contacted by Reuters were in a range of between A$143 million to A$147 million.
Analysts said the tight range of forecasts was unsurprising as the group had already announced that its sales rose 8.61 percent to A$8.22 billion in the 28 weeks to January 5.
First half food sales were up 8.60 percent, general merchandise up 9.50 percent and specialty retail up 4.92 percent.
Retail analyst at Prudential-Bache Securities (Australia) Ltd, John Burgess, said he was forecasting a first half net profit of A$144.5 million.

Burgess said his forecast was based on the stable pricing environment in Australia which allowed the company's sales growth to be converted into EBIT growth but diluted slightly by a higher interest expense.
"Unlike most retailers, Woolworths' market has been growing very strongly and they have been taking share in that market," Burgess said.
"(Woolworths') supermarkets are continuing to introduce fresh produce in more and more stores and are taking away share from the specialty shares," he said.
Rebecca King, retail analyst at ANZ Securities is forecasting half year net profit of A$146.8 million.
Last month, Woolworths chief executive Reg Clairs told Reuters he expected the company the company to report a satisfactory first half result.
"It would appear it's going to be a satisfactory result, but I can't really predict that until all the numbers are in," he said in an interview.
Clairs said Woolworths hoped to maintain sales growth in the second half of 8.0 to 8.5 percent.
